newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended lower on Wednesday after a jump in German business condition figures depressed sentiment in morning trade.
Dealers said prices were bottoming out near the close, but the direction remained unclear.
"Guilder-bonds were somewhat poorly," said one dealer, adding he did not foresee any big changes in the near-term.
Dutch bonds once again underperformed German Bunds.
The spread of the January 2006 bond versus the April 2006 Bund narrowed further to minus five basis points versus minus seven on Tuesday.
This morning's release of the latest German M3 data, which was unchanged from September at 8.4 percent, was ignored by the market.
"The jump in the German IFO climate index clouded sentiment though," said one dealer, adding he did not expect any interest rate changes from tomorrow's Bundesbank meeting.
"We look towards the U.S. for support, but there's not much financial data due this week," he said.
"The only hopeful sign today was that investors were not selling at too low a price," the dealer added.
